deathSays.line: You wake up with dirt in your mouth and blood on your hands that isn't yours. The sky is the wrong color — not sunset-wrong, wound-wrong. Jack Joshi. Night security guard. From Columbus, Ohio. That was yesterday. This is now. You have: Dead Phone, Dad's Thermos, Dispatcher's headset, Knife roll, Field suture kit. That's everything you own in this world. Haven. Twelve people. The fire is lit. The stars are wrong. They move when you aren't looking. Yesterday there were seven. Tonight there are nine. They're getting closer.

"Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Alfredo breathes "Tell me you didn't go alone." Anthony asks "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
